noodles/f51cab4:
The chain audit's 24-roll distribution showed every hot roll's sample
peak sitting exactly at the 0.64 ceiling while reconstruction rang
2.2-3.75 dB past the clipped tops: the ceiling's own flat edges were
manufacturing the true-peak problem, concentrated in the bright funk and
garage kits, worst roll -0.13 dBTP. The fix is one argument into
makeShaper - the ceiling waveshaper runs at 4x oversampling, native
browser resampling, curve untouched - so the clipper holds down the
peaks the DAC will actually reconstruct instead of only the ones the
sample grid can see.

true peak -0.13 to -1.76 dBTP with zero rolls above -1.5 (was 4); CAL
fixture tp -0.75 to -2.45; render cost none/2x/4x = 291/313/302 ms per
rendered second with differences inside trial noise, measured on a
pinned-vibe harness after an unpinned first pass claimed +24% and turned
out to be measuring the cold open's random vibe; audit harmonics table
byte-identical at every drive level; calibrate deterministic rows within
the documented 0.1 dB noise floor; smoke green. Sample peaks read -2 to
-3 now instead of pinning at -3.88 - the samples showing the
reconstruction honestly rather than hiding it between them.

copycats/f50bb2d:
SimVersus holds a whole match as an append-only log of placements and
input-log entries; scores, pools, fates, and standings all derive from
replaying it. That log is the future relay wire format - a couch match
and an async match are the same object at different paces - and
resume-after-reload just re-derives from the saved log.

Rules: everyone places one object, everyone runs the same locked house
against the shared pool of past lives (never this round's rivals - the
reveal is the resolution), finishers score one plus a first-dinner
bonus, both nulled when everyone lands on their feet. Any cat or
copycat killed by an object credits its owner, always. Swatted pool
ghosts are removed; each run joins its owner's pool, capped at two.
First to nine. Matches are device-local, so concurrent matches on
different devices are isolated by construction.

find_killer() extends fate computation with kill attribution (which
item, hence which owner), and launcher tracks carry their item index.
The shell gains the couch setup screen, per-pelt cats (eight pelts,
names as the identity system), turn banners, handoff screens, the
all-at-once resolution playback with named swat pops, standings, and
autosave to user://couch.save.

run_couch_flow.gd drives a full three-cat round through the real scene
headless: setup, placements, three runs, playback, standings, round 2.
The solo golden checksum is unchanged.
